title: Traders can profit from both rising and falling prices
claim: Traders can profit from rising (long) or falling (short) prices, enabling profit across market conditions.
support: Direct author assertion with EUR-USD/USD examples.
mechanism: Long trades capitalize on appreciation; short trades profit from depreciation.

title: Technical analysis works via crowd psychology
claim: Markets driven by millions of participants whose buying/selling reflects consistent emotional patterns (greed, fear).
support: Author argues emotions constant across centuries and regimes.
mechanism: Self-fulfilling prophecy: millions using same concepts leads to convergent action.

title: Candlestick charts convey more information than line charts
claim: Candlesticks display OHLC for each period, capturing intra-period fluctuations line charts miss.
mechanism: Body shows open-close; wicks show full range; enables intra-period pattern recognition.

title: Pinbar reversal at S/R
claim: Pinbar (small body, long wick) at support/resistance signals reversal opportunity.
mechanism: Wick rejects extreme; S/R provides resistance.

title: Doji as indecision marker
claim: Doji (open=close, long wicks) represents indecision and precedes reversal at extremes.
mechanism: Equal open/close indicates balance; reversal likely.

title: Price waves characterize all trends
claim: All movements decompose into upwaves and downwaves; uptrends have steeper upwaves than downwaves.
support: Detailed explanation with wave ratio figures.
mechanism: Uptrend = buyers dominate; upwaves faster than corrections.

title: Swing points as inflection markers
claim: Swing highs/lows mark wave endpoints and provide S/R anchors.
support: Definition with examples; basis for S/R analysis.
mechanism: Swing points represent collective decision points where trend pauses.

title: Head-and-Shoulders reversal
claim: HAS (left shoulder, head, right shoulder at neckline) predicts uptrend-to-downtrend reversal.
mechanism: Diminishing peaks indicate exhaustion; neckline break confirms.

title: Ascending Triangle bullish breakout
claim: Ascending Triangle (horizontal resistance + rising floor) indicates bullish bias; upside break is signal.
mechanism: Rising lows show buyers; horizontal resistance = exhaustion; break confirms.

title: Trend line break signals reversal
claim: Confirmed trend line (3+ touches) break preceded by swing changes signals reversal.
support: Detailed explanation with high/low changes before break.
mechanism: Break indicates market structure shift; swing changes confirm weakening.

title: Support/Resistance as reversal zones
claim: S/R zones (3+ reversals) act as inflection points for reversals or consolidation.
support: S/R mechanics explanation with multiple-touch figures.
mechanism: Market participants place orders at known zones; collective density creates stickiness.

title: Confluence increases trade probability
claim: Multiple signals (candlestick, trend line, S/R, patterns) converging increases win rate.
support: Explicit author statement; double-low spring example (engulfing at double-low).
mechanism: Multiple signals increase trader awareness and order clustering.

title: Moving Average five signals
claim: MAs provide: crossover, slope, distance, S/R, rate-of-change signals for trend confirmation.
support: Enumeration of five signals by author as foundation.
mechanism: MA smooths noise; slopes/crossovers indicate momentum; distance shows strength.

title: RSI divergence precedes reversal
claim: RSI divergence (price new high but RSI not) often precedes trend reversal.
support: Author statement on divergence as signal.
mechanism: Divergence indicates weakening momentum despite price movement.

title: Bollinger Bands measure volatility
claim: Bollinger Bands (2-std envelope) provide dynamic S/R; extreme touches suggest reversals.
support: Definition and usage as trend-following and reversal tool.
mechanism: Bands expand high-vol; contract signals breakout; extremes suggest reversal.

title: MACD crossover signals momentum shift
claim: MACD line/signal crossover and histogram divergence signal momentum changes and entries.
mechanism: MACD reflects momentum; crossover confirms shift; divergence indicates weakening.

title: Pattern memorization without mechanics limits adaptability
claim: Traders memorizing patterns without understanding buyer/seller dynamics fail when context changes.
support: Author critique of conventional pattern-memorization books.
mechanism: Static matching fails when conditions shift; mechanics enable adaptation.

title: Trend line subjectivity requires confirmation
claim: Trend lines are subjective; traders should confirm with confluence (S/R, swings).
support: Author warning on subjectivity; recommendation for confluence.
mechanism: Multiple valid lines possible; confluence improves reliability.

title: Indicator redundancy wastes monitoring
claim: Avoid stacking indicators measuring same concept; redundant indicators add clutter without new signal.
support: Author on indicator groups and redundancy.
